--- title: "[Graph.select_nodes_by_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Select top-K nodes by centrality measure. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L11386-L11535){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.select_nodes_by_centrality( measure="degree", k=10, include_ties=False, **kwargs, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Select nodes by centrality](/assets/graphs/select-nodes-by-centrality.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The six-node grid with an extra diagonal edge B–D, each node badged with its PageRank score. B scores highest at 0.24, ahead of D and E at 0.18, so selecting the top one node by PageRank selects B, drawn in the accent color." width="100%"} Computes a centrality score for every node, ranks the nodes from highest to lowest score, and adds the top `k` to the current node selection. It combines a centrality computation and a selection step in one call, so the most important nodes can be acted on directly with the `*_ws` methods. Typical uses: - highlighting or labelling the most influential nodes before plotting - extracting the core of a network with `transform_to_subgraph_ws()` - targeted-attack robustness experiments, deleting the top hubs with `delete_nodes_ws()` and measuring how the graph falls apart The measures differ in what "important" means: degree counts direct connections, PageRank rewards links from other important nodes, and betweenness rewards nodes that sit on many shortest paths. Degree-based measures are cheap; betweenness computes all-pairs shortest paths and can be slow on large graphs. Note that `"pagerank"` and `"betweenness"` also store their scores as a node attribute (`pagerank` and `betweenness_centrality` by default), exactly as calling `pagerank()` or `betweenness_centrality()` would. Selection is cumulative, so call `clear_selection()` first to start fresh. The graph is modified in place and returned for chaining. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [measure]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["degree"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Centrality measure used for ranking. One of `"degree"` (default; total degree, i.e. in-degree plus out-degree for directed graphs, as returned by `get_degree()`), `"in_degree"` or `"out_degree"` (directed graphs only; `ValueError` otherwise), `"pagerank"` (see `pagerank()`), or `"betweenness"` (see `betweenness_centrality()`). Any other value raises `ValueError`. [k]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[10]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of top-ranked nodes to select. Defaults to `10`. If `k` is at least the number of nodes, every node is selected; `k=0` selects nothing. [include_ties]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Controls what happens when several nodes share the score at the cut-off. If `False` (default), exactly `k` nodes are selected and ties at the boundary are broken arbitrarily, so which of the tied nodes is chosen is not guaranteed. If `True`, every node whose score is at least the `k`-th highest score is selected, so the result can contain more than `k` nodes. [**kwargs]{.doc-parameter-name} : Extra keyword arguments forwarded to `pagerank()` when `measure="pagerank"`, e.g., `damping=`, `max_iter=`, `tol=`, or `attr_name=` (to change the name of the stored score attribute). Passing an argument that `pagerank()` does not accept raises `TypeError`. For all other measures, `**kwargs` is ignored. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The same graph (modified in place) for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `measure=` is unknown, or if `"in_degree"` or `"out_degree"` is used on an undirected graph. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} In this graph "A" has degree `3`, "B" and "C" are tied at `2`, and "D" has degree `1`. Asking for the top two by degree selects "A" plus one of the tied pair, so the count is exactly `2`: ::: {#ca7da5ae .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("A", "C"), ("A", "D"), ("B", "C")]) .select_nodes_by_centrality("degree", k=2) ) graph.count_selected_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: With `include_ties=True`, both "B" and "C" are kept because they share the score at the cut-off, so the selection grows to three nodes and is deterministic: ::: {#42143907 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.clear_selection() graph.select_nodes_by_centrality("degree", k=2, include_ties=True) sorted(graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in graph.get_selected_node_ids()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ['A', 'B', 'C'] ``` ::: ::: Extra keyword arguments are forwarded to `pagerank()` -- here `damping=` is passed through. In this directed graph every other node links to "hub", so it ranks first: ::: {#c28ae596 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} web = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["hub", "p1", "p2", "p3"]) .add_edges([("p1", "hub"), ("p2", "hub"), ("p3", "hub"), ("hub", "p1")]) .select_nodes_by_centrality("pagerank", k=1, damping=0.85) ) [web.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in web.get_selected_node_ids()] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` ['hub'] ``` ::: ::: As a side effect, the PageRank scores computed for the ranking are stored on the nodes, so they can be inspected in the node table afterwards: ::: {#c0f4fe1e .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} web.get_node_df().select("label", "pagerank") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
